speaker: Doctor
text:
Let me start by asking: how long have you noticed this breast mass, and has it changed in size or texture since you first noticed it?

REQUEST TEST: Mammography
REQUEST IMAGES: Breast_Mammogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast.

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very strange; Gastroenteritis is an intestinal infection and cannot cause a breast mass. Given the rapid increase in size, we must rule out malignancy or an aggressive infection immediately. Please confirm if you have any fever, chills, or recent weight loss. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC) and ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: Breast_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), Heart Rate 72 bpm. Complete Blood Count (CBC) and ESR: NORMAL READINGS (no fever or signs of acute infection). Breast Ultrasound: Complex, heterogeneous, hypervascular mass with irregular margins in the left breast upper outer quadrant. Biopsy: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor (likely Benign or Borderline given the lack of necrosis/hemorrhage mentioned, but cellular overgrowth is concerning).

Given the ultrasound showing leaf-like structures with stromal overgrowth and normal inflammatory markers, this is not an infection. Do you have a history of similar lumps in your family, and would you like me to recommend a surgical excision plan?
